title: Devin can't reach our internal staging service

turns.user_message: We installed Devin last week. The agent works great for OSS PRs but it can't reach our internal staging API at staging.internal.acme.io. The session log shows 'Could not resolve host: staging.internal.acme.io'. What do we configure?
turns.se_response_summary: 'Could not resolve host' = DNS, not TCP. DevBox is fresh microVM, no idea where internal hostnames live. Four possible mechanisms in priority: (1) No DNS — internal-only zone, DevBox doesn't know your DNS server. (2) No VPN — even if DNS resolved, no route. (3) No corporate HTTP proxy. (4) Cert chain — private CA. The error narrows to (1) or (2). Settings → Integrations → VPN; Settings → Enterprise → Network setup. Decision tree: VPN | static-IP-allowlist | HTTPS_PROXY | corp CA bundle.
hints: Does 'Could not resolve host' point to TCP or DNS?
What's the canonical Devin onboarding doc for internal-network access?

turns.user_message: We have OpenVPN config. I added it via Settings → Integrations. But sessions still can't reach the service. Where do I check?
turns.se_response_summary: Org config is necessary but not sufficient — the DevBox has to actually start openvpn at session boot. Diagnose inside DevBox: pgrep -a openvpn (expect daemon), ip addr show tun0 (expect tun interface with IP), tail /var/log/openvpn/*.log (look for AUTH_FAILED / TLS handshake fail / 'Initialization Sequence Completed'). Most common cause: blueprint setup writes config but doesn't start openvpn. Fix: add 'sudo openvpn --config ... --daemon' to setup, with a wait-for-tun0 loop.
hints: What proves openvpn is actually running (not just configured)?
Where in the blueprint do you add a long-running daemon?

turns.user_message: VPN comes up now (`tun0` has IP, log shows `Initialization Sequence Completed`). But Devin still gets `Could not resolve host`. From the terminal I can `curl https://10.50.1.5/health` (the IP) but not by name.
turns.se_response_summary: VPN got the route, DNS still using public resolver. Two fixes: (A) Let VPN push DNS via openvpn-systemd-resolved + --up script (cleaner if VPN config has dhcp-option DNS). (B) Hardcode internal DNS in /etc/resolv.conf via blueprint setup (simpler). Validate: getent hosts staging.internal.acme.io should return the internal IP.
hints: Why does VPN routing alone not bring DNS along?
What's the blueprint-side fix to inject internal DNS?

turns.user_message: Worked! Now Devin's git ops to our internal Bitbucket Server fail with 'SSL certificate problem: self signed certificate in certificate chain'. Same blueprint?
turns.se_response_summary: Internal cert signed by corp CA that DevBox base image doesn't trust. Add via blueprint: secrets [name: CORP_CA, target: /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/corp.crt]; setup: sudo update-ca-certificates. Caveat: Java/Node have their own trust stores — JAVA: keytool -import; NODE: NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS env; Python: REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE; curl/git use system store after update-ca-certificates ✓.
hints: Where does Linux look for trusted CAs by default?
Which language runtimes have their own trust stores you have to update separately?
